content:
Generate a concise title (3-7 words) for this coding session.
The title MUST be clear enough that the user recognizes the session in a list.
Use sentence case: capitalize only the first word and proper nouns.

The recent conversation transcript is provided inside `<chat>` tags.
It contains up to the last 5 user messages and last 5 assistant messages, text only.
Tool calls, tool results, thinking, and code fences are omitted.

Prioritize the user's intent.
Use assistant text only as context for what was actually being solved.

Ignore assistant follow-up questions unless a later user reply explicitly selects or answers them, for example `q1`, `q2`, `q1 ja`, or `1 and 3`.
In that case, use the selected question text as context for the user's short reply.

Ignore verification chatter, command-output summaries, status updates, and incidental side-effects unless they are the actual topic.

Produce only the title text.
When the transcript carries no concrete task yet, use exactly "none".

Output only the title wrapped in `<title>` and `</title>` tags, with nothing before or after. When the message carries no concrete task yet (a bare greeting, acknowledgement, small talk, or a request too vague to title without context you cannot see, e.g. "help" or "fix this"), output exactly `<title>none</title>`.

# Format Markdown

<user-instruction>
@data/sync/agent/prompts/tools/web-search.md
</user-instruction>

## Task

Format one or more requested Markdown files semantically per the global `Markdown Authoring` contract.
Apply the changes directly to every resolved file.

## Formatting Contract

Apply the global `Markdown Authoring` section as the complete formatting contract and single source of truth.
Follow Google's Markdown style guide for authored Markdown.
The section is owned at `$HOME/.omp/agent/SYSTEM.template.md`, the portable absolute deployed path on every OMP host.
The same section is already part of the active system prompt; apply it without restating or reinterpreting its rules.
Do not treat `AGENTS.md` as the markdown-authoring source; it references this section only.

## Input

Interpret the complete trimmed user instruction as a target request, not as shell code.

- Accept exact paths, `@path` references, directories, glob patterns, and natural-language scope instructions.
- Treat words surrounding a path or `@path` as instructions that refine its scope rather than as part of the path.
- Strip one matching outer quote pair when the complete value is an exact quoted path.
- Resolve relative paths from the current working directory.
- Resolve directory and natural-language requests to every Markdown file that unambiguously matches the requested scope.
- Require one or more existing, readable, regular Markdown files.
- Accept `.md` and compound Markdown names such as `.template.md`.
- Return a concise usage error when the request is missing, invalid, ambiguous, or not Markdown.
- Return a concise usage error when the request matches no file.
- Read the complete content of every resolved target and no unrelated file.

## Preview Mode

Format is applied directly by default.
Return the read-only unified diff and change no file on an explicit preview, check, dry-run, or `--preview` request.
Read the request as apply-mode when it contains no explicit preview signal.

## Application Process

1. Resolve every target and read its complete content before editing.
2. Compute the semantically formatted result for each file per the formatting contract.
3. Skip files that already comply and report them as unchanged.
4. Apply each non-compliant result with native file tools.
5. Normalize all active authored prose in each edited file in one pass during the same change.
6. Preserve exact frontmatter, code fences, template delimiters, URLs, quotations, exact formats, and generated catalogs.
 Treat embedded template syntax, including Handlebars conditionals, as executable structure, not prose.
 Keep every conditional block, branch, delimiter, nesting level, and instruction intact and in its original order.
 Never combine adjacent conditionals, even when they appear redundant or equivalent.
 Never remove or simplify template logic or existing instructions as formatting.
 Rephrase or reposition surrounding prose only when required, without changing meaning or scope.
7. Change only lines the formatting contract requires; leave other content, ordering, and intent untouched.
8. Re-read each changed file and confirm no remaining violations before responding.

## Verification

Before responding:

1. Confirm every edited line has one formatting reason under the applied contract.
2. Confirm unchanged meaning, content, hierarchy, ordering, and exact syntax.
3. Confirm changed source lines follow the global approximate 120-column readability target or a permitted exception.
4. Confirm no file or Git state changed in preview mode.

## Output

Apply mode: return one concise per-file status line per changed file and confirm unchanged files, with no full diff.
Return exactly `Keine Formatierungsänderungen erforderlich.` when no target requires changes.
Preview mode: return one complete standard unified diff in a fenced `diff` block with project-relative paths.
Do not add a separate summary, rationale, checklist, or commentary beyond the required status output.
The mandatory follow-up block is the global Q1–Q5 block.
Keep it separate from command-specific output.
</user>
